cases.title: CDRENUMBER lists P9 -> P8 and P10 -> P9, No changes nothing, Yes renumbers the two pits, the Pit Schedule follows, and U brings the old numbers back
cases.expected: On the untouched copy CDRENUMBER says the main outlet is not obvious and asks 'Which pit is the main outlet? ... [C1/X1] <C1>:' (answered C1), lists 'Renumber downhill to uphill:', 'P9 -> P8' and 'P10 -> P9', and asks '2 pit(s) will be renumbered. Apply? [Yes/No] <No>:'. No prints 'Renumber cancelled - nothing changed.'. Run again and Yes prints 'Renumbered 2 pit(s) downhill to uphill. One Undo restores the old numbers.'; the Pit Schedule then lists Pit P8 and no Pit P10; two U (the first echoes PITSCHEDULE, the second CDRENUMBER) and the schedule lists Pit P10 again and no Pit P8.
cases.why_not_unit: The network walk runs on the real drawing's pits and pipes and writes every label in one live command; the schedule is read from the live drawing.
not_automated: The PIT LABEL blocks on the plan are not read one by one (their handles are not known); the Pit Schedule rows are read instead. The non-P marks (C1, AGI, TG, WT) are checked only by recording the schedule before and after.
Whether the network order chosen is the right engineering order is not judged (the preview is taken as CE's rule; Tim's word for the rule itself).
